news.title: Odisha RERA asks promoters to furnish updated occupancy, CC details within 30 days
news.para: The Odisha Real Estate Regulatory Authority has set new guidelines requiring promoters to upload updated certificates within thirty days of receipt. Non-compliance could lead to penalties and potential restrictions on property registration. Additionally, promoters seeking approval must present proof of application and payment. This initiative is designed to promote transparency and safeguard the interests of homebuyers.

news.title: Reliance MET City appoints Manish Jaiswal as CEO; Embassy Developments names Neel Virwani as CBO
news.para: Reliance MET City has appointed Manish Jaiswal as chief executive officer to lead its business and growth strategy. Embassy Developments has appointed Neel Virwani as chief business officer, effective October 1, 2026, to drive expansion across North and West India.

news.title: Andhra Pradesh government to set up special cell to clear hurdles to high-rise building plans
news.para: The state government is enhancing the approval process for tall buildings by establishing a specialized unit for applications pertaining to structures with five or more floors. This initiative seeks to expedite review timelines and minimize holdups for developers. Authorities are tasked with addressing existing software issues and promoting transparency. These reforms are designed to invigorate the construction and real estate sectors statewide.

news.title: Convert B khata to A until end of 2027: Karnataka government
news.para: Karnataka government has authorized the conversion of eligible 'B' Khata properties to 'A' Khata. This new mechanism will be implemented by urban and rural development departments until December 2027. Properties up to 1,000 square meters with proposed non-agricultural use are covered by this order. Specific cut-off dates apply for properties in urban and rural local bodies respectively.

news.title: Housing project in Haryana’s Sultanpur park buffer zone seeks fresh wildlife clearance
news.para: A developer is pursuing wildlife clearance for a new housing development close to Sultanpur National Park. This comes on the heels of a committee uncovering multiple infractions within the eco-sensitive region. The firm claims that their project aligns with the zonal master plan. However, environmental advocates argue that existing violations must be addressed before any further construction can be approved.

news.title: Chandigarh administration proposes 50% rate for freehold conversion
news.para: The Chandigarh administration has put forth a proposal to transition leasehold properties into freehold status. The conversion charges will be set at fifty percent of the collector rate, while properties acquired through auctions will incur a twenty-five percent fee. This initiative has been forwarded to the Ministry of Home Affairs, and the administration is now awaiting its review and approval.

news.title: Green future: Cement makers accelerate decarbonisation push
news.para: In a significant shift towards sustainability, Indian cement manufacturers are enhancing the use of green energy and implementing efficiency improvements. By adopting waste heat recovery systems, these firms are not only curbing energy usage but also lowering operational costs. Additionally, they are expanding their renewable energy capacities, aligning with long-term carbon reduction goals, while exploring innovative carbon capture technologies for future integration.

news.title: NGT seeks Haryana response over Mayfield Gardens construction violations
news.para: The National Green Tribunal is calling on Haryana officials to address reported breaches of environmental regulations. These allegations involve unauthorized construction activities and illegal extraction of groundwater. The tribunal has instructed relevant authorities to cease all unlawful building activities immediately. Previous grievances highlighted similar issues to the Union environment ministry. The next session to discuss this critical environmental matter is set for November sixteenth.

news.title: MCD demolition drive continues across Delhi, 213 demolitions carried out this month
news.para: On Sunday, the Municipal Corporation of Delhi executed eleven property demolitions and enforced the sealing of four locations. This initiative is part of a concerted effort to tackle unsafe and unauthorized constructions, a drive that has intensified following a tragic building collapse that resulted in the deaths of seven individuals.

news.title: Telangana assembly okays CURE Bill, caps revision of property tax at 10%
news.para: On Saturday, the Core Urban Region Bill was passed by the Telangana assembly, significantly cutting the property tax revision limit from twenty percent to ten. The BJP opposed this legislation and sought its retraction, whereas AIMIM requested the bill's referral to a select committee. Conversely, the CPI party expressed their support for the bill proposed by the legislative affairs minister.

news.title: Six lakh property owners yet to pay ₹848 crore tax in Chennai
news.para: Greater Chennai Corporation has urged over six lakh property owners to clear their tax dues.  The civic body is awaiting ₹847.80 crore in pending property tax collections.  Property tax funds essential civic services like roads and public health initiatives.  Owners must pay property tax every half-yearly period before the deadline.  Failure to pay will attract interest on outstanding amounts from the next period.

news.title: Odisha RERA mandates buyer-promoter presence at CDR hearings
news.para: The Odisha Real Estate Regulatory Authority has mandated that parties attend conciliation hearings in person. This new rule is designed to enhance the effectiveness of dispute resolution and minimize delays. Both promoters and complainants are expected to be present to foster meaningful discussions and arrive at decisions. The conciliation cell strives to facilitate amicable resolutions between homebuyers and developers, ensuring that proceedings conclude promptly without unwarranted postponements.

news.title: Prayagraj development body plans ‘Tulsi Vihar’ housing scheme on reclaimed Kareli land
news.para: The Prayagraj Development Authority is set to breathe new life into the encroached lands with the launch of 'Tulsi Vihar', a residential project that aims to restore the historical essence of the Tulsipur area. Alongside this, potential homeowners can take advantage of enticing discounts on more than 400 available flats, enjoying waivers and early payment bonuses of up to eighteen percent. Allotments will be prioritized on a first-come, first-served basis.

news.title: Not a brick has moved in 21 months: Supertech buyers hit the streets, say will march to Parliament next
news.para: Homebuyers of Supertech's halted projects are voicing their frustration over construction delays. They are insisting on an immediate revival of work along with definitive completion timelines. Although NBCC was designated as the project management consultant more than twenty-one months ago, no significant construction progress has occurred, despite repeated court orders, leaving buyers disheartened and anxious.

news.title: Panchkula civic body seals six buildings without approved maps
news.para: In a bid to uphold building regulations, the Panchkula Municipal Corporation has sealed six buildings found to be constructed without sanctioned plans. Following thorough inspections, civic officials identified multiple violations of municipal laws. MC commissioner Vinay Kumar underscored the importance of systematic urban development, asserting that efforts will be made to ensure compliance and deter unauthorized construction with ongoing inspections and enforcement actions.

news.title: Ahmedabad civic body offers nine plots worth ₹1,010 crore with FSI, height details
news.para: The Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation has announced an auction for nine city plots, each featuring distinct development criteria. With a combined base price exceeding one thousand crore rupees, these plots present a lucrative opportunity for developers. Interested parties are encouraged to gauge their potential as they prepare to submit bids during this multi-day online auction process, designed to enhance builder engagement and facilitate urban growth.

news.title: April–Aug property registrations in Maharashtra jump 12% over last year, revenue up nearly 16%
news.para: In the first five months of the 2026-27 fiscal year, Maharashtra's property registrations saw a significant increase of 12.4%. The region's revenue collections experienced an impressive rise of nearly 16%, reaching Rs 26,637.73 crore. Steady transaction activity, particularly high-value deals, has fueled this growth. As the festive season approaches, officials anticipate that this positive momentum will further invigorate the property market.
